If you didn't get Megaton when it was available, this is an absolute no-brainer classic FPS worth getting without a doubt.

Randy Pitchford is a very weird man, and "Duke Nukem 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour" is the result of his hubris. This may be incorrect, that's hard to say, but due to how outpoken he was about this whole ordeal, hard to think otherwise. 

The developers just updated the original Build Engine, but since Randy Pitchford was not able to get neither Nightdive nor Ken Silverman (the original creator of the engine),  work was relegated to Nerve Software, one of their last projects. The result is not very good; the game has a lot of new bugs. I had quite a few deaths for no good reason.

The new textures a mixed bag, some of them look nice, most of them make no difference, but some are awful. At least of the animated textures is not animated in this game. The lightning is shockingly bad, some places are so dark to the point that it's easier to turn off the "remastered" mode and see what I am actually doing. 

The new voices are controversial, but I think they're fine. You can tecnically select the original voices, but the volume is so low that it's just not worth it.

The reason why you would buy this version instead of the one that exists at the Zoom Platform would be the commentary and the new episode.

They're both terrible. Randy tried to do what Valve did with half life, and failed miserably

Since there are no subtitles, it's impossible to know who is talking on each snippet. Only 5 people participate in the commentary, 4 of them are level designers and one of the programmers of this specific version, sp no commentary of the musicians, artists or even the original programmers. The commentary seems to be one session of the developers playing the game, with no preparation whatsoever. These people do not remember anything from their own maps, so the commentary consists of them cracking jokes about how "bad" the levels of the original games were, complaining about their own decisions while creating the game.

It's funny, because the new episode is so much worse than the original.

The levels by design have no continuity among themselves, differently from the original 3 episodes. It's supposed to be an adventure all around the world, but it feels disjointed. One of the levels has one part that you're not supposed to be in until you go somewhere else, according to the commentary. The penalty is dying. Quoting the actual designer of this level, "I hope you have saved".
I really hate the idea of killing the bosses of the original episodes as not-so-common enemies, it devaluates them as a  end-of-an-episode threats.
Speaking of the enemies, the new ones are awful. The Firefly Trooper is just awful, baffling to the point of absurdity. They're the only ones that original, and they barely appear at the game, so they know this is awful.
The overlord and cycloid sentries are just the original bosses sprites and programming recycled. The Cycloid Incinerator is far more bizarre; he is a recycled Cycloid Emperor, but with a weapon with a very low range. As long as you keep your distance, he will not kill you. Trivial to the point of hilarity

A part of the cult classics such as Doom, Quake and Marathon, the Duke Nukem games are a must-have to add to your collection. It has been fun replaying this game since I was younger. All the new features knocked the dust off this classic and brought it back to life for today's platforms. I replayed every level, including the secret levels that I had discovered. A lot of action. [b]Features :[/b]

- Playback : When enabled, you can rewind after dying or making a mistake. Or you can decide to use saves.

- Render Mode : Selecting this while in-game toggles original source code rendering and 2.5D engine re-mastered rendering in True 3D.

- Developer Commentary : When enabled, you can find little icons throughout the levels that can be toggled to hear developer comments.

- New Episode : Alien World Order created by original Duke Nukem designers, Allen Blum and Richard “Levelord” Gray.

- New Enemies : Firefly Troopers, Overlord Sentries, Cycloid Sentries and a new final boss, the Cycloid Incinerator.

- New Weapon : The Incinerator.

- New Audio : A new soundtrack for Alien World Order was composed by Lee Jackson, original composer for the game's 1996 release. In addition, Duke's one-liners have been re-recorded by voice actor Jon St. John, and some of the sound effects have been updated.

- Multiplayer : Co-op, Dukematch and DM-Bots.

[b]Save Folder Location :[/b]

The saves can be found in the "Gearbox" folder, which is located in :

C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Local

%appdata%\..\Local\
( copy/paste that line in your file explorer and hit enter )

Locate the "Gearbox" folder and right-click copy and paste to a safe location.

The new re-recorded voices are spot on, but i think it's a shame all other sound effects didn't get the same modern audio touch up. There's a mod that replaces the bit-crushed effects with their source ones, which combined with the new re-recorded lines results in crisp audio presentation above any other port. The new commentary by the devs is also cool, shedding light on limitations and original design that didn't get into the final version.

DUKE NUKEM 3D is an amazing classic FPS and an absolute must play for any boomer shooter lover. Duke's attitude and the vibe of this game never fail to make me smile because they perfectly embodies the classic action hero, and crank it up to 11. Level and enemy design are stellar throughout, and the new 5th episode added to this remaster is an amazing addition to this game! Duke's suite of weapons manage to be both fleshed out and really fun, and distinct from the iconic DOOM weapon roster. In particular, the shotgun, chaingun, rocket launcher and devastator are some of my favorite boomer shooter weapons of all time.

Aside from the addition of a brand new episode created by the original level and music designers, this 20th Anniversary World Tour addition of the game does have some drawbacks. Most notably, this version lacks numerous famous expansion packs, such as Life's a Beach, Duke It Out in D.C., Nuclear Winter, and a few others. It's also generally a little buggy, especially the vertical mouse aim. I noticed a few audio glitches as well, and I couldn't map certain in-game actions to my mouse buttons successfully. It's a shame that Gearbox and Randy Pitchford own the rights to the DUKE NUKEM IP, because they have continually mismanaged this franchise and it deserves SO much better.

I personally am too lazy to install a source port and play this amazing game in its superior form. The negatives about this port of the game are not nearly enough to keep me away because this game is amazing! DUKE NUKEM 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour Edition regularly goes on sale for $2.99, which is honestly so worth it. I highly recommend this classic game. Play it in whatever way you can.

This game is the purest distillation of what it was like to be alive in the 90s. At least, it is by my reckoning. I was born in 2001 but I'm fairly sure about this.

Was blown away of how mechanically complex this 1996 game is. A jump button , an inventory with multiple helpful choices (like a medikit or a hologram that confuses the enemies), breakeable walls, great graphics and cutscenes. And for this rerelease, they made a whole new episode 5, with the same level designers and even brought back Duke's voice actor, Jon St. John. Also added a dev commentary mode, which is always a good thing.
But for the actual gameplay: you shoot aliens, while collecting key cards to advance through the level. What makes it unique compared to the others from that time is the great weapon selection. There's the standard meele, pistol, shotgun, rocket leuncher and chaingun. The other weapons are fantastic, a shrink gun, a freeze gun, pipe bombs, a laser trip mine and a new one in episode 5, the incinerator. All of them are useful and makes the combat feel fluid.
My favorite part was Duke's voicelines, with them being cheesy one-liners and pop culture references, which this game has a lot of. Although I felt a bit weird seeing these almost naked womens captured, but I could look past that.
If you like fps games from that era, then give it a shot, you won't regret it.

Reseña de Duke Nukem 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour

Duke Nukem 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour es una versión modernizada de uno de los shooters más legendarios y polémicos de los años 90. Esta edición busca mantener intacta la esencia clásica de Duke Nukem mientras agrega mejoras visuales, nuevo contenido y soporte para plataformas modernas.

La historia sigue nuevamente a Duke Nukem enfrentando una invasión alienígena llena de caos, explosiones y humor exagerado. Como siempre, la narrativa funciona más como una excusa para lanzar al jugador a niveles llenos de acción y secretos.

El gameplay sigue siendo increíblemente divertido incluso hoy. Duke Nukem 3D mantiene esa mezcla clásica de velocidad, exploración y combate arcade donde constantemente encuentras armas absurdas, pasajes ocultos y situaciones completamente exageradas.

Uno de los mayores atractivos es la personalidad de Duke. Sus frases, actitud arrogante y humor absurdo ayudaron muchísimo a convertirlo en un ícono de los videojuegos de los 90.

La versión 20th Anniversary incluye mejoras visuales opcionales, nuevos episodios y comentarios de los desarrolladores originales. Además, la nueva campaña agrega mapas bastante entretenidos para fans veteranos.

El diseño de niveles sigue siendo excelente. Los escenarios están llenos de secretos, rutas alternativas y elementos interactivos que hacen la exploración muy entretenida.

Las armas también continúan siendo muy memorables, especialmente la escopeta, el lanzacohetes y la famosa Shrink Ray.

Sin embargo, varios aspectos claramente envejecieron. El humor puede sentirse demasiado exagerado o anticuado para algunos jugadores modernos y ciertas mecánicas ya no tienen la misma fluidez comparadas con shooters actuales.

Además, algunos problemas técnicos y ciertas decisiones de esta edición recibieron críticas por parte de fans clásicos.

Visualmente el juego mantiene gran parte de su estética retro, algo que encantará a muchos jugadores nostálgicos pero puede alejar a quienes buscan gráficos modernos.

Aun así, Duke Nukem 3D sigue siendo una pieza fundamental en la historia de los FPS y esta edición continúa siendo una forma muy entretenida de experimentar uno de los shooters más importantes de los años 90.

Calificación: 8.5/10

Recomendo demais! Duke Nukem 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour é um daqueles clássicos dos shooters em primeira pessoa que ainda entrega diversão pura mesmo depois de tantos anos. Você assume o papel de um herói exagerado, sarcástico e cheio de atitude que vai salvando a Terra de alienígenas invasores com muito estilo e frases marcantes. A campanha é dividida em episódios com níveis cheios de segredos, caminhos alternativos e um level design inteligente que realmente recompensa quem explora cada canto.

O gameplay é rápido, direto e absurdamente satisfatório. As armas têm um peso ótimo, os inimigos são variados e as interações com o ambiente são um destaque, como chutar objetos, quebrar paredes ou usar o jetpack para alcançar lugares altos. Tudo flui com aquela energia old school que faz você se sentir poderoso enquanto avança destruindo tudo pelo caminho. Essa versão de aniversário traz melhorias visuais, suporte a widescreen, novos episódios exclusivos e até um editor de mapas, o que deixa a experiência mais completa.

Os gráficos foram atualizados com texturas mais nítidas e iluminação melhorada, mas mantêm todo o charme retrô original. A trilha sonora rockeira combina perfeitamente com o clima divertido e exagerado. Os diálogos e o humor ácido ainda funcionam muito bem e trazem vários sorrisos durante as partidas.

No final, é uma ótima forma de jogar ou rejogar esse ícone dos anos 90 com qualidade moderna. Se você curte shooters clássicos, level design criativo e uma experiência sem frescura, cheia de ação e personalidade, vai fundo. Nota 8.5/10. É daqueles jogos que envelheceram com dignidade e ainda divertem bastante.

[h1]J'ADORE DUKE NUKEM mais prenez la version gratuite EDUKE32[/h1]

Cette version est malheureusement décevante. La molette ne fonctionne plus, le bouton d’action répond de manière aléatoire, la 4K a disparu, et des éléments clés comme Holoduke ou les excellentes extensions de la Megaton Edition ont été supprimés.

Du coup on a droit à quoi en plus sur la version originale ? Une tentative d’ajout de lumière dynamique, qui améliore légèrement la lisibilité des textures, mais au prix de nombreux artefacts visuels. Egalement un nouveau chapitre qu'ils ont survendu, mais se révèle vide et excessivement linéaire : pas de jetpack, des combats répétitifs contre des vagues d’aliens a la manière d'un Serious Sam, tout est mal calibré jusqu'au ratio vie/munition, tout est sans subtilité. Le boss final achève le tout : une simple recoloration d’un ancien ennemi, inoffensif, qui crache des flammes. Difficile de faire plus paresseux. Il vous restera donc les commentaires de l'ancienne équipe, tous inintéressants et spammés absolument partout au premier niveau, mais en vrai vous n'en reverrai plus jamais après ça de tout le jeu ! Parce qu'ils assument complètement de vous avoir arnaqué.

L’ensemble donne une impression de travail bâclé. On sent une volonté d’exploiter la licence plus que de la respecter, mais bon c'est Gearbox Software, ils n'ont jamais vraiment respecté grand chose. Ils avaient de l'or entre les mains mais c'est un immense gâchis.

À choisir, mieux vaut se tourner vers EDuke32 : les fans ont fait un travail bien plus sérieux et c'est gratuit.

I have no proper explanation for this. It very consistently does absolutely nothing if you try to scroll while moving, but it also frequently fails if you try to switch while doing nothing else at all. I decided to test this by sitting still and rapidly scrolling up and down and it just occasionally switched one gun forward without ever going backward. The action in this game is fast paced and demands frequent gun-switching, making this a game-breaking problem. Super disappointing :(
